source.title: Chebyshev Sets, Klee Sets, and Chebyshev Centers with respect to Bregman Distances: Recent Results and Open Problems

accepted.question_text: Let X = R^n, let f: X -> [-infinity, +infinity] be a convex Legendre function, let U = int dom f, and let C be a nonempty closed subset of U. The Bregman distance induced by f is D(x, y) = f(x) - f(y) - <grad f(y), x - y> for y in U. The set C is called left D-Chebyshev when, for every y in U, the left nearest-points map P_left,C(y) = {x in C | D(x, y) = inf_{z in C} D(z, y)} is a singleton. It is known that if f is supercoercive and C is left D-Chebyshev, then C is convex. Is the supercoercivity assumption actually necessary for that convexity conclusion?
accepted.context_brief: Necessity of supercoercivity for left D-Chebyshev convexity

evidence.quote: Definition 1.7 (Chebyshev sets) The set C is a left Chebyshev set with respect to the Bregman distance, or simply <-D-Chebyshev, if for every y in U, <-PC(y) is a singleton.
Fact 3.1 (<- D-Chebyshev sets) (See [7, Theorem 4.7].) Suppose that f is supercoercive and that C is <-D-Chebyshev. Then C is convex.
Problem 1. Is the assumption that f be supercoercive in Fact 3.1 really essential?

accepted.question_text: Let X = R^n, let f: X -> [-infinity, +infinity] be a convex Legendre function, let U = int dom f, and define the Bregman distance D(a, b) = f(a) - f(b) - <grad f(b), a - b> for b in U. Let C be a nonempty closed subset of U, let C* = grad f(C), and let U* = int dom f*. The set C is right D-Chebyshev when, for every x in U, the map P_right,C(x) = {y in C | D(x, y) = inf_{z in C} D(x, z)} is a singleton. If dom f = X, C* is contained in U*, and C is right D-Chebyshev, then C* is known to be convex. Are the full-domain assumption on f and the containment C* subset U* both genuinely necessary for that convexity conclusion?
accepted.context_brief: Necessity of the assumptions in Fact 3.2

evidence.quote: Definition 1.7 (Chebyshev sets) ... the set C is a right Chebyshev set with respect to the Bregman distance, or simply ->D-Chebyshev, if for every x in U, ->PC(x) is a singleton.
Fact 3.2 (->D-Chebyshev sets) (See [7, Theorem 7.3].) Suppose that dom f = X, that C* subseteq U*, and that C is ->D-Chebyshev. Then C* is convex.
Problem 2. Are the assumptions that f have full domain and that C* subseteq U* in Fact 3.2 really essential?

accepted.question_text: Let X = R^n, let f: X -> [-infinity, +infinity] be a convex Legendre function with full domain X, and define the Bregman distance D(a, b) = f(a) - f(b) - <grad f(b), a - b>. A nonempty closed convex subset C of X is right D-Chebyshev if every x in X has a unique point y in C minimizing D(x, y). Does there exist such an f that is not quadratic, but for which every nonempty closed convex subset of X is right D-Chebyshev? Equivalently, can a nonquadratic full-domain Legendre generator have a nonaffine gradient map that nevertheless preserves convexity strongly enough to make all nonempty closed convex subsets right D-Chebyshev?
accepted.context_brief: Existence of nonquadratic full-domain right D-Chebyshev geometry

evidence.quote: Fact 3.4 (See [6, Lemma 3.5].) Suppose that f is the negative entropy (see Example 1.1(ii)) and that C is convex. Then C is ->D-Chebyshev.

Fact 3.4 raises two intriguing questions. Apart from the case of quadratic functions, are there instances of f where f has full domain and where every closed convex subset of U is ->D-Chebyshev? Because of Fact 3.2, an affirmative answer to this question would imply that grad f is a (quite surprising) nonaffine yet convexity-preserving transformation.

Problem 3. Does there exist a Legendre function f with full domain such that f is not quadratic yet every nonempty closed convex subset of X is ->D-Chebyshev? In view of Fact 3.1, the gradient operator grad f of such a function would be nonaffine and it would preserve convexity.

accepted.question_text: Let X = R^n_{++} be the strictly positive orthant, and let f be the negative entropy Legendre function whose Bregman distance is the Kullback-Leibler divergence on positive vectors. A subset C of X is right D-Chebyshev when every x in X has a unique y in C minimizing D(x, y). Closed convex subsets are known to be right D-Chebyshev in this setting, and there also exist nonconvex right D-Chebyshev subsets. Can one characterize exactly which subsets of the strictly positive orthant are right D-Chebyshev for this negative-entropy Bregman distance?
accepted.context_brief: Characterizing right D-Chebyshev sets for negative entropy

evidence.quote: Fact 3.4 (See [6, Lemma 3.5].) Suppose that f is the negative entropy (see Example 1.1(ii)) and that C is convex. Then C is ->D-Chebyshev.

Combining Example 3.3 and Fact 3.4, we deduce that - when working with the negative entropy - if C is convex, then C is ->D-Chebyshev but not vice versa. Is it possible to describe the ->D-Chebyshev sets in this setting?

Problem 4. Is it possible to characterize the class of ->D-Chebyshev subsets of the strictly positive orthant when f is the negative entropy? Fact 3.4 and Example 3.3 imply that this class contains not only all closed convex but also some nonconvex subsets.

accepted.question_text: Let X = R^n, let f: X -> [-infinity, +infinity] be a convex Legendre function, let U = int dom f, and define the Bregman distance D(a, b) = f(a) - f(b) - <grad f(b), a - b> for b in U. For a nonempty closed subset C of U, let P_left,C(y) be the set of points in C minimizing D(., y). Suppose f is twice continuously differentiable and the Hessian grad^2 f(y) is positive definite for every y in U. If f is additionally supercoercive, then P_left,C is known to be single-valued almost everywhere and generically on U. Is the supercoercivity assumption genuinely necessary for this almost-everywhere and generic single-valuedness conclusion?
accepted.context_brief: Necessity of supercoercivity in near-Chebyshev single-valuedness

evidence.quote: Fact 3.5 (See [7, Corollary 5.6].) Suppose that f is supercoercive, that f is twice continuously differentiable, and that for every y in U, grad^2 f(y) is positive definite. Then <-PC is almost everywhere and generically single-valued on U.
It would be interesting to see whether or not supercoercivity is essential in Fact 3.5.
Problem 5. Is the assumption that f be supercoercive in Fact 3.5 really essential?

accepted.question_text: Let X = R^n, let f: X -> [-infinity, +infinity] be a convex Legendre function, let U = int dom f, and define the Bregman distance D(a, b) = f(a) - f(b) - <grad f(b), a - b> for b in U. For a bounded nonempty closed subset C of U, let Q_left,C(y) be the set of points in C maximizing D(., y). Suppose f is twice continuously differentiable and the Hessian grad^2 f(y) is positive definite for every y in U. If f is additionally supercoercive, then Q_left,C is known to be single-valued almost everywhere and generically on U. Is supercoercivity genuinely necessary for this almost-everywhere and generic single-valuedness conclusion?
accepted.context_brief: Necessity of supercoercivity for near-Klee single-valuedness

evidence.quote: Fact 4.4 (See [7, Corollary 5.2.(ii)].) Suppose that f is supercoercive, that f is twice continuously differentiable, that for every y in U, grad^2 f(y) is positive definite, and that C is bounded. Then <-QC is almost everywhere and generically single-valued on U.
Again, it would be interesting to see whether or not supercoercivity is essential in Fact 4.4.
Problem 6. Is the assumption that f be supercoercive in Fact 4.4 really essential?

accepted.question_text: Let X = R^n and let g: X -> [-infinity, +infinity] be a proper lower semicontinuous function. In the Euclidean theory of Chebyshev and Klee functions, the discrepancy is q(x) = (1/2)||x||^2, the halved Euclidean distance squared. What are the corresponding characterizations when that Euclidean discrepancy is replaced by a Bregman distance generated by a Legendre function f? In particular, how should one characterize the admissible generator f and the associated Chebyshev point in the Bregman-distance setting?
accepted.context_brief: Bregman analogues of Chebyshev and Klee functions

evidence.quote: Chebyshev set and Klee set problems can be generalized to problems involving functions. Throughout this section, g : X -> [-infinity, +infinity] is lower semicontinuous and proper.
For convenience, we also set q := 1/2 ||.||^2.
Problem 7. For the Chebyshev functions and Klee functions, we have used the halved Euclidean distance. What are characterizations of f and Chebyshev point of f when one uses the Bregman distances?

accepted.question_text: Within the finite-dimensional Euclidean framework X = R^n for Chebyshev functions and Klee functions, results concern single-valuedness, characterizations, and Chebyshev-point behavior for proper lower semicontinuous functions. How can those results be extended to Hilbert spaces, or even to general Banach spaces?
accepted.context_brief: Extending Chebyshev and Klee function results to Hilbert and Banach spaces

evidence.quote: Chebyshev set and Klee set problems can be generalized to problems involving functions.
Facts 7.5 and 7.7 below concern Chebyshev functions and Klee functions; see [37] for proofs.
Problem 8. How do the results on Chebyshev functions and Klee functions extend to Hilbert spaces or even general Banach spaces?
